propositions: rebar cannot reconcile against self-hosted Jira Data Center because it lacks DC-specific transport for REST v2, wiki/plain-text bodies, PAT auth, and name-based user identity

PR #120's second-adapter approach creates an unsustainable shared-library pattern by reaching into adapters/jira privates and forking map_fields_to_remote, leaving no contract pinning what is shared and allowing Cloud changes to break DC silently

Field-map and sanitizer logic exists in multiple independent copies across adapters/jira/jira_fields.py, adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py, and rebar_reconciler/config.py, with documented drift (deleted key disagreement) that a single shared definition must resolve

Location-pinned modules (adf.py, outbound_fields.py, comment_limits.py) loaded by file path via dynamic loader cannot relocate to a new sub-package without breaking the loader and all mock.patch sites, but their contents can be edited to import from a shared layer via dependency inversion

DC must reject non-https base_url unless explicitly overridden with allow_insecure=true, never disable TLS certificate verification, require JIRA_PAT only from environment (never config file), and support operator-configured workflow state names via reconciler.resolved_statuses to avoid misclassifying resolved issues

A machine-checked import contract (CI-enforced, not conventional) must forbid cross-imports between adapters/jira and adapters/jira_datacenter while permitting both to import from adapters/jira_family, preventing the drift this epic exists to eliminate
